newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan interbank rate ends up on stock rally.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan interbank rate ends up on stock rally.

text.p: Taiwan's interbank rate closed sharply higher on Thursday as investors siphoned funds out of the banking system into the sizzling stock market, where turnover spiked to a record T$297 billion, dealers said.
Liquidity was further tightened by the central bank's ongoing mop-up measures, including the absorption on Thursday of T$10 billion through a state bank.

The overnight interbank rate closed at 7.720 percent against Wednesday's 7.437 close -- well outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone but still below the record double-digit closes of late June.
Central bank Governor Sheu Yuan-dong has said the bank would not adjust monetary policy merely to cool the bourse, saying money supply was no economic cure-all.
Sheu nevertheless has made clear that the central bank would continue to fine-tune money supply through NCDs, treasury bills and other methods of intervention.
In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 5.9900-6.0000.
